title: Refactor add-on entitlement matrix and contract UI for enterprise security bundles
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Enterprise customers are requesting clearer entitlements and a simpler contract flow when purchasing observability retention, compliance packs (security questionnaire responses + audit logging), and premium SLA uplift. Current experience scatters these options across billing, support, and a separate feature toggle matrix, causing sales & legal friction and manual contract edits.

Objective: Consolidate add-on entitlements into a single matrix surfaced in the Contract Builder UI and the self-serve upgrade flow; wire entitlement flags into billing and telemetry; provide a one-click export of security questionnaire answers and contract clauses for legal review. This should enable a gated rollout for premium observability retention tiers, a discrete compliance pack SKU, and an SLA uplift product that can be toggled per-account in dedicated and private deployments.

Scope:
- UX: Contract Builder: new Add-on Matrix panel with checkboxes, brief descriptions, SKU codes, and pricing preview.
- Backend: entitlement flag service updated to support per-account addon SKUs and contract-embedded metadata.
- Billing: prorated billing and invoice line item mapping for upgrades/downgrades.
- Legal/Security: templated contract clauses and automated security questionnaire export (CSV + PDF).
- Console: telemetry dashboards showing adoption and latency/cost correlations for observability retention.

Out of scope (this ticket): implementation of on-prem installer changes for Private deployments (handled in ENG-18912) and deep audit log storage tiering beyond retention controls.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Bundling observability retention as a clearly priced addon will increase paid upgrades from mid-market customers by 18% within 90 days.
- H2: Providing templated security questionnaire answers will reduce legal review cycle time by ~30% per contract.

Success metrics:
- 15% uplift in conversion from trial to paid for teams with >100k tokens/month within 90 days of rollout.
- Median legal review time for new enterprise contracts reduced from 7 days to 5 days.
- No regression in API SLOs; retention addon telemetry must show <5% increase in 95th pct latency for typical workloads.

Stakeholders: Sales (Christine Cole), Legal (Maya Singh), Security (Ethan Wu), Billing (Priya Nair), Console UX (Liam O'Connor), Serving Eng leads (Sasha Petrov).

Key constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Entitlement gating at subscription-level vs. per-route: subscription-level gating chosen to keep contract language simple and reduce billing complexity.
- Retention tiering granularity: selected 30/90/365-day tiers as a compromise between customer flexibility and storage/cost predictability for us.
- SLA uplift as an additive SKU vs. included in enterprise: we'll surface as additive to enable a pricing experiment with sales.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged beta for 5 existing enterprise customers (sales-nominated) -> iterate based on legal/billing feedback -> wider pilot with sandboxed Contracts team -> GA behind standard entitlement rules and pricing page entries.
acceptance_criteria: Contract Builder shows Add-on Matrix and allows selection of observability retention tiers (30/90/365) with price preview
Entitlement flags created in backend per-account and visible in Console entitlement page
Billing system emits correct prorated invoice line items for mid-cycle addon upgrades/downgrades
Security questionnaire export generated automatically from templated answers and attached to contract draft
SLA uplift SKU applied to account without requiring manual legal amendment
Instrumentation: adoption and latency telemetry dashboards created and populated for pilot accounts
